dissent: All six baseline findings are editorially resolved. The full round-1 snapshot produced no clear additional editworthy inconsistency under these five stored lenses.

Preserve the deliberately severe magic prices, costly resealing, truthful but self-interested God, brutal politics and real loss. The review supports clear boundaries, not harmless sorcery or an automatic rescue.

The ordinary spell-exhaustion option is demanding enough to deserve eventual playtest attention, especially for a caster-heavy party; this static review neither verifies balance nor labels the cost a failure.
The authored structure remains a declared tradeoff with Harper/Baker emergent-play preferences. Core-clue reliability should not settle the God's ultimate nature or compel every parallel lead.
No human or generated runtime playtest, pacing measurement, normalization test or successful ending execution was performed by this panel review. No one-hour target applies.

priorityActions: No further editorial changes requested by these four lenses after a full revision-one reread.
Preserve the fixed coffer states, actual-access requirements, inspectable costs and conditional aftermaths through later revisions.
Runtime narration, comprehension and pacing remain untested.
dissent: Le Guin's cost/consequence lens does not require that the God's own exchanges use the same currency as ordinary casting; the explicit replacement bargain preserves clarity.
Leiber supports supernatural uncertainty and a freed power beyond faction command. A safe immediate release location need not guarantee a benevolent future.
Jemisin's structural reading accepts that neutral custody leaves baronial rule intact; every ending need not repair the society.
Abercrombie's resistance to unearned comfort does not require incurable illness, inevitable betrayal or loss of every cherished memory. Preserve contingent, earned outcomes.

findings.title: Clarify how release succeeds at the deliberately dry alternative site

basis.application: Applied only to the stated source-supported concern; no claim of actual player response.

blueprintEvidence.quote: draws water from every unsealed well or vessel within sight to form a walking body of brine
Covering supplies or choosing a dry, evacuated basin prevents those immediate losses. It can leave thereafter;
release in a prepared dry site avoids that loss but frees a power no faction controls.

findings.reason: The safe-site alternative is explicitly promised, but the only stated formation mechanism requires the water that preparation removes. A narrator could infer either failed release or a substitute water source, changing a consequential informed choice. This is a small missing causal bridge, not a reason to remove the safe preparation option.
findings.recommendation: State the dry-site manifestation (for example, a thin body from brine already inside the cage) and confirm that covered supplies and living bodies are outside the draw. Keep release irreversible and the entity independent.
findings.mitigation: The rules already fix physical release, exclude universal command, warn about visible unsealed sources and honor preventive preparation.
findings.confidence: High confidence in the wording gap; no observed runtime failure. Parent independently raised the same clarification.

findings.title: Finale conflates opening the shell with releasing the God

basis.application: Applied only to the stated source-supported concern; no claim of actual player response.

blueprintEvidence.quote: Opening beside an occupied well endangers its water;
then deliberately lift the bar.
it cures Corr's wasting sickness in exchange for opening its outer shell, revealing the inner bar but not lifting it;

findings.reason: The bounded cure deliberately opens only the shell, while the water draw is a consequence of release after lifting the inner bar. The finale shorthand can therefore attach release damage to the permitted lesser act. This matters precisely when a player accepts the stated cure while safeguarding the cage.
findings.recommendation: Replace the finale warning with “Releasing the God beside an occupied well endangers its water” (or equivalent), retaining the explicit shell/bar distinction.
findings.mitigation: Rules 2 and 4 already provide the correct distinction and the final hint says to use only physically possible choices and learned costs. A one-word alignment is sufficient.
findings.confidence: High textual confidence; no runtime assertion.

uncertainty.limits: Composite evidence review, not an interview or playtest. Narration, persistence, voice behavior and pacing were not exercised. No one-hour target applies.
uncertainty.dissent: A costly imperfect ending is compatible with G1-G3; it need not repair the entire political order or promise eternal containment. Narrated rules are not proof of mechanically enforced persistence.
uncertainty.verificationQuestion: If Corr accepts the shell-opening cure and the inner bar remains down, does the actual scene preserve nearby water and record the cure accurately?
